title: The Microduck's electronic roster — every component, what it is, how big it is, what it draws, what it weighs
by: microduck night shift, lane C (electronics verification)
why_this_file_and_not_elec-spec.json: The lane brief said to extend electronics/elec-spec.json. That file cannot take these rows: ce-elec's loader REFUSES any key outside its fixed roster — ce-elec/elec/levels.py:39 SPEC_KEYS and :105-113, verbatim 'spec %r carries keys this tool does not read ... A key silently ignored is a requirement silently dropped.' Adding `components` there would break `bin/elec levels` for this design. So the roster lives here, elec-spec.json's notes point at it, and both stay loadable.
what_this_file_holds_and_what_it_does_no: It holds ONLY what the triad shelf does not: the physical envelope parsed into numbers, mass, quantity, role, where it is fitted, and each row's open items. Identity, package quote, datasheet URL and revision, supplies, current, I2C address, pinout and logic levels are NOT copied here — tools/gen_electronics_datasheet.py reads them live out of ce-parts/<slug>/electrical.*.json and component.json, because TRIAD.md says apps never hold product truth. A number that appears twice drifts; a number that appears once does not.
precision_rule: Dimensions are recorded to the number of decimals the SOURCE states and no further. Where a datasheet prints '5.00 mm' that is what appears; where it prints '5 x 5 mm' the trailing zeros are not invented. A dimension nobody published is null with a `why`.

components.name: Radxa ZERO 3W
components.role: Application processor board — Rockchip RK3566 quad Cortex-A55, the host for robotd/tofd/mediad
components.fitted_where: head, under the Robot HAT (MJCF body jaw_soft; the simulator's stand-in mesh is pcb__raspberry_pi_zero_2_w)

dimensions_mm.z_why: PCB THICKNESS IS NOT DIMENSIONED in RAD-DOC-0084. cad/part.py builds 1.6 mm, measured off Pollen's Pi-Zero-2-W STAND-IN mesh, not off a Radxa.
dimensions_mm.source: Radxa ZERO 3W Product Brief RAD-DOC-0084 Rev 1.10 (2026-06-26) §4 Mechanical Specification, document p.5 = PDF page 6, printed callouts '65. 0' and '30. 0'. Local copy ce-parts/radxa-zero-3w/iterations/v0.0.1/docs/fetched/radxa_zero_3w_product_brief.pdf, sha256 edfb01374bbc6ee4062adf50d5d7241de64b64c8e87d186b3577bbb8761ddead, fetched 2026-09-02 from https://dl.radxa.com/zero3/docs/hw/3w/radxa_zero_3w_product_brief.pdf
dimensions_mm.dp_why: Decimals as the SOURCE prints them (components.json precision_rule): Radxa's callouts read '65. 0' and '30. 0' — one decimal each. Axes with no dp are ones this file has no printed precision for; they fall back to %g.

components.mount_pattern: 4 x Ø2.8140 mm on 57.8429 x 22.8662 mm, 3.5727 mm edge inset — MEASURED off §4's raster by tools/measure_radxa_drawing.py (4/4 negative controls PASS); Radxa prints only '4 X Ø2. 8' and one '3. 6'. Full frame: ce-parts/radxa-zero-3w/iterations/v0.0.1/cad/interfaces.json
components.mass_why: CANNOT DETERMINE. Radxa states no weight in the Product Brief, the wiki, or the product page (checked 2026-09-02); ameridroid's listing carries no weight either (fetched 2026-09-02). The bare-FR4 5.7329 g that ce-cad reports when it builds this part is volume x FR4 density and EXCLUDES every component, so it is not the board's mass. A scale on a production board settles it.
components.power_note: 5 V in, on the USB 2.0 OTG Type-C port or GPIO pins 2/4 — §5.1 p.5 verbatim: 'Power adapter with 5V/2A on the USB 2.0 OTG Type-C power port', '5V Power from the GPIO PIN 2 & 4'. On the Microduck the 5 V comes up through the HAT from the pack.
components.current_why: CANNOT DETERMINE at every operating point — idle, policy running, and camera+H.264 encode. No Radxa document states board current. A meter in the 5 V path settles it, and it is the single missing number in the whole power budget.
open: SKU (see ce-parts/radxa-zero-3w electrical.host.json identity_vs_fitted): Radxa offers no 1 GB + 32 GB eMMC row.
Which corner of the 40-pin header is pin 1 — not dimensioned, and a HAT laid out the wrong way round is scrap.

components.mass_note: 99 g is 12.7 % of the robot's 780 g. Together with the 270 g of servos, 47.3 % of the machine is accounted for by two line items.

voltage.source: THE ROBOT'S OWN WINDOW, not a vendor's: research/raw/duck-control_src_model.rs:109-112 BATTERY_FULL_V = 8.2 / BATTERY_EMPTY_V = 6.6, mapped linearly to 0-100 %.

WHICH pack (maker, cell, protection IC, UN 38.3 / IEC 62133-2 marks): CANNOT DETERMINE.
The bay's tightest clearance is 0.0145 mm, against the contact PCB. A pack 0.1 mm longer than Pollen's model does not go in.
Contact pinout: no vendor drawing of an NP-F contact face was found.
components.mass_representative_why: 99 g is the shipping weight of a Duracell DR5 'replacement NP-F550' — a DIFFERENT pack from the one Pollen fits. It is carried as the best available figure and marked everywhere it appears; the FITTED pack's mass is CANNOT DETERMINE and one scale settles it.

mass_budget.$about: What the roster can and cannot account for. The robot's total is a vendor claim, not a weighing.
mass_budget.robot_total_source: Pollen store listing, '25 cm tall, 780 g' (research/raw/store_microduck.json, fetched 2026-09-02)

accounted.basis: Duracell DR5 page, 99 g — a representative pack, not the fitted one

mass_budget.unaccounted_note: 411.0 g — 52.7 % of the robot — is printed parts, fasteners, bearings, cables, and every board and module whose mass is CANNOT DETERMINE. The printed parts are sliced and weighed elsewhere in this repo (218 g PLA + 26 g TPU, out/print/), which leaves roughly 167 g for fasteners, bearings, harness and all the electronics. NOT ONE electronic board or module in this roster has a published or measured mass.
mass_budget.what_would_close_it: A scale, and one production robot stripped.
mass_budget.representative_note: One of the two accounted lines is not a mass of this robot: the 99 g battery figure is a vendor shipping weight for a REPRESENTATIVE NP-F550-form pack, not the fitted one. Take the accounted total as 270 g measured-or-vendor-for-the-fitted-part plus 99 g representative, and the unaccounted 411 g as a floor rather than a figure.

open_items.what: Three custom PCBs have no design files
open_items.settles_it: Design them (lane D) or obtain Pollen's. Nothing else in this roster blocks a build as hard as this.

open_items.what: The Robot HAT must carry an audio power amplifier that nobody has published
open_items.settles_it: An ohmmeter across the fitted speaker's leads, plus a teardown photo of the HAT.

open_items.what: The ToF socket must regulate and level-shift, because it has to accept either generation
open_items.settles_it: Identifying the breakout, or measuring the voltage on the Stemma J5's 3V3 pin on a production robot.

open_items.what: The servos run 0.6-2.2 V above their rated maximum with the over-voltage shutdown disabled
open_items.settles_it: A meter on servo VDD at full charge. Then a thermal test at 8.2 V, or a regulator.

open_items.what: Board current is unmeasured everywhere — Radxa, HAT, imu_to_dxl
open_items.settles_it: A meter in the 5 V path and on the bus. Until then the ~1 h runtime claim cannot be checked against 18.7 Wh.
